framework: Virginia state academic standards: Personal Finance
subject: Personal Finance

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge and integration of basic economic concepts and structures by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge and integration of basic economic concepts and structures by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge and integration of basic economic concepts and structures by

outcomes.text: describing how consumers, businesses, and government decision makers face scarcity of resources and must make trade-offs and incur opportunity costs;
explaining that choices often have long-term, unintended consequences;

describing how effective decision making requires a comparison of the additional costs (marginal costs) and additional benefits (marginal benefits), using a cost- benefit analysis chart and PACED decision-making grid (i.e., state the problem; list alternatives; identify the criteria; evaluate the alternatives based on the criteria; make a decision) for economic and personal finance decisions;
describing the factors of production;
comparing the characteristics and applications of market, command, traditional, and mixed economies; and
identifying Adam Smith and describing the characteristics of a market economy.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of producers and consumers in a market economy by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of producers and consumers in a market economy by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of producers and consumers in a market economy by (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: describing how consumers, producers, workers, savers, investors, and citizens respond to incentives;
explaining how businesses respond to consumer sovereignty;
identifying the role of entrepreneurs;
comparing the costs and benefits of different forms of business organization, including sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, franchise, and cooperative;
describing how costs and revenues affect profit and supply;

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of producers and consumers in a market economy by (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: describing how increased productivity affects costs of production and standards of living;
examining how investment in human capital, capital goods, and technology can improve productivity;
describing the effects of competition on producers, sellers, and consumers;
explaining why monopolies or collusion among sellers reduces competition and raises prices; and
illustrating the circular flow of economic activity.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the price system by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the price system by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the price system by

outcomes.text: analyzing the laws of supply and demand and the determinants of each;
explaining how the interaction of supply and demand determines equilibrium price and wages;
describing the elasticity of supply and demand; and
examining the purposes and implications of price ceilings and price floors.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the many factors that affect income by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the many factors that affect income by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the many factors that affect income by

outcomes.text: examining the market value of a worker’s education, skills, training, knowledge, and credentials;
identifying the impact of human capital on production costs;
explaining the relationship between a person’s own human capital and the resulting income potential;
performing an analysis of expenses and financial aid required for continuing education to expand human capital; and
describing how changes in supply and demand for goods and services affect income.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of a nation’s economic goals, including full employment, stable prices, and economic growth by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of a nation’s economic goals, including full employment, stable prices, and economic growth by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of a nation’s economic goals, including full employment, stable prices, and economic growth by

outcomes.text: distinguishing among economic indicators, for example, gross domestic product (GDP), consumer price index (CPI), and unemployment rate;
analyzing the causes and effects of unemployment, inflation, and reduced economic growth;
describing the fluctuations of the business cycle and how economic indicators change throughout the business cycle; and
describing strategies for achieving national economic goals.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the nation’s financial system by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the nation’s financial system by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the nation’s financial system by

outcomes.text: comparing the role of money and currency;
explaining the roles and types of financial markets and financial institutions;
describing the purpose, structure, and function of the Federal Reserve System, including the role of monetary policy;
identifying the tools of monetary policy (e.g., Fed funds rate);
comparing the U.S. monetary system with the international monetary system; and
explaining how certain historical events have influenced the banking system and other financial institutions.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of how fiscal policy influences employment, output, and prices by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of how fiscal policy influences employment, output, and prices by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of how fiscal policy influences employment, output, and prices by

outcomes.text: describing government’s role in stabilizing the economy through congressional spending and tax policy;
describing sources of government revenue; and
explaining balanced budget, deficit, and national debt.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of government in a market economy by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of government in a market economy by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of government in a market economy by

outcomes.text: identifying goods and services provided by government to benefit society;
identifying the role government plays in providing a legal structure to protect property rights and enforce contracts;
providing examples of government regulation of the market; and
explaining that governments redistribute wealth.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the global economy by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the global economy by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the global economy by (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: explaining that when parties trade voluntarily, all benefit;
distinguishing between absolute and comparative advantage;
distinguishing between trade deficit and trade surplus;
explaining exchange rates and the impact of the strength of the dollar on economic decisions;

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the global economy by (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: describing the costs and benefits of trade barriers;
describing the effects of international trade agreements and the World Trade Organization; and
explaining growing economic interdependence.

units.title: The student will develop consumer skills by

topics.title: The student will develop consumer skills by

subtopics.title: The student will develop consumer skills by (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: examining basic economic concepts (such as scarcity and opportunity cost) and their relation to product prices and consumer spending;
describing common types of contracts and the implications of each;
demonstrating comparison-shopping skills;
examining the importance of maintaining a system for personal financial records;

subtopics.title: The student will develop consumer skills by (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: examining the impact of advertising and marketing on consumer demand and decision making in the global marketplace;
accessing reliable financial information from a variety of sources;
explaining consumer rights, responsibilities, remedies, and the importance of consumer vigilance; and
examining precautions for protecting identity and other personal information.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of planning for living and leisure expenses by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of planning for living and leisure expenses by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of planning for living and leisure expenses by (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: comparing the costs and benefits of purchasing vs. leasing a vehicle;
calculating the total costs of owning and operating a vehicle;
comparing the costs and benefits of renting vs. purchasing a residence;
describing the process of renting a residence;

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of planning for living and leisure expenses by (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: describing the process of purchasing a residence;
calculating the cost of utilities, services, maintenance, and other residential expenses; and
evaluating discretionary spending decisions.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of banking transactions by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of banking transactions by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of banking transactions by

outcomes.text: evaluating services and related costs associated with personal banking;
differentiating among types of electronic monetary transactions;
preparing all forms necessary for opening and maintaining a checking and a savings account;
reconciling bank statements;
comparing costs and benefits of online and traditional banking; and
examining how financial institutions affect personal financial planning.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of credit and loan functions by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of credit and loan functions by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of credit and loan functions by (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: evaluating the various methods of financing a purchase;
analyzing credit card features and their impact on personal financial planning;
identifying qualifications needed to obtain credit and the information needed to complete a credit application;
examining basic provisions of credit and loan laws;
comparing terms and conditions of various sources of consumer credit;

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of credit and loan functions by (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: identifying strategies for effective debt management, including sources of assistance;
explaining the ways to build and maintain a good credit rating and the ramifications of an individual’s credit score;
comparing the costs and conditions of secured and unsecured loans;
comparing the types of voluntary and involuntary bankruptcy and the implications of each; and
comparing amortization schedules for a loan based on principal, time, annual percentage rate (APR), and different credit ratings.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of insurance in risk management by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of insurance in risk management by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of the role of insurance in risk management by

outcomes.text: identifying different ways to manage risk;
evaluating insurance as a risk management strategy;
distinguishing among the types, costs, and benefits of insurance coverage, including identity theft, automobile, life, property, and health; and
examining potential ramifications of lifestyle choices on premiums, insurability, and employability.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of income earning, taxes, and reporting by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of income earning, taxes, and reporting by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of income earning, taxes, and reporting by (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: differentiating among sources of income;
calculating gross and net pay;
investigating employee benefits and incentives (e.g., pretax savings opportunities);
describing the types and purposes of local, state, and federal taxes and the way each is levied and used;
exploring how tax structures affect individuals of different income levels;

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of income earning, taxes, and reporting by (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: computing local taxes on products and services;
explaining the content and purpose of a standard W-2 form;
completing standard employment tax forms; and
describing information relevant to the completion of state and federal income tax forms.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of personal financial planning by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of personal financial planning by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of personal financial planning by (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: identifying short-term and long-term personal financial goals;
identifying anticipated and unanticipated income and expenses;
defining terminology associated with inheritance and estate planning;
examining components and purposes of a personal net worth statement;

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of personal financial planning by (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: developing a personal budget;
investigating the effects of government actions and economic conditions on personal financial planning; and
explaining how economics influences a personal financial plan.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of investment and savings planning by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of investment and savings planning by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of investment and savings planning by

outcomes.text: comparing the impact of simple interest vs. compound interest on savings;
comparing various options for investment and savings;
examining the fundamental workings of Social Security and the system's effects on retirement planning;
comparing various options for long-term planning (e.g., Virginia529 Plan, retirement plans); and
describing how the stock market works.

units.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of financing postsecondary education by

topics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of financing postsecondary education by

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of financing postsecondary education by (1 of 3)

outcomes.text: identifying costs and benefits of postsecondary education;
identifying sources of postsecondary education funding;
identifying the purpose of the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) in determining eligibility for grants, scholarships, and loans and the essential information needed to complete it;
describing types of aid which do not require repayment, including federal, state, and institutional grants;
describing types of scholarships and identifying scholarship scams;

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of financing postsecondary education by (2 of 3)

outcomes.text: examining types of student loans, including federal and private, and understanding the associated risks;
examining the requirements to remain eligible for financial aid;
explaining repayment requirements and options for student loans, including income-appropriate repayment plans and options for loan forgiveness, cancellation, and discharge;
describing the options for borrowers struggling to make payments and the consequences of failure to repay student loans;

describing benefits, eligibility requirements, and tax implications of state- sponsored tax-advantage-qualified tuition plans as investment options for postsecondary education (e.g., Virginia529 Plan);

subtopics.title: The student will demonstrate knowledge of financing postsecondary education by (3 of 3)

outcomes.text: identifying the multiple pathways to postsecondary education and career preparedness;
identifying parts of a financial award letter;
identifying the student loan default rates of postsecondary institutions in Virginia;
describing appropriate income levels needed to support student loan borrowing.
